chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'One who eats clay and dies, he has aided upon himself.'

key_terms.أَعَانَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ: He aided upon himself (hastened his own death)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating clay according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith establishes the principle of 'self-inflicted harm' (ikhlāf al-nafs), where consuming clay is viewed as a direct cause of death unless an underlying pathology is present. Shia scholars often contextualize this within the broader legal maxim of 'no harm' (lā darar), distinguishing between habitual consumption for sustenance or medicinal purposes versus excessive intake leading to demise. It serves as a foundational text for understanding how physical actions can be legally categorized as self-sabotage in Islamic jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘One who eats the clay, so he dies, so he has aided upon himself’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘
If one eats clay and dies he has helped to kill himself.’”
